headline: The customer never says what refund she wants on each of 16 disputes, yet the official answer fixes specific values (including a $69.99 partial refund), and which two disputes get provisional credit depends on an unstated counting rule and filing order.

issues.summary: resolution_requested (and partial_refund_amount) is a persisted field the KB says to ask the customer for, but the user instructions give no resolution for any of the 16 disputes. Gold fixes XFINITY to partial_refund 69.99 from a vague 'around $120', and AT&T to full_refund even though the customer was 'promised a partial refund'.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_014: "13. resolution_requested (string) - Ask user what resolution they want."
instructions: "XFINITY $189.99 on 10/28/2025 - INCORRECT AMOUNT. Your usual bill is around $120."
instructions: "AT&T Business $312.50 ... were promised a partial refund weeks ago" vs gold[24] "resolution_requested": "full_refund"
instructions: "Tesla Supercharger $67.45 ... You were overcharged" vs gold[22] "full_refund"
tools.py file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 stores resolution_requested and partial_refund_amount in transaction_disputes
issues.why_it_matters: The user simulator has to make up each resolution. If it asks for 'about $70' back on XFINITY, or for the partial refund AT&T promised, the stored dispute record differs from gold and the DB hash fails. Whether the agent matches comes down to how the simulator happens to improvise.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the resolution for each dispute to the user instructions (e.g. 'XFINITY: partial refund of $69.99; all others: full refund'), or change gold[24] to match the AT&T partial-refund story.

issues.summary: doc_015 criterion 4 does not say whether disputes filed earlier in the same session count toward the 'more than 2 disputes in 12 months' limit. Under the running-count reading only the first two new filings qualify, and which two depends on filing order. The customer states her priority (Staples, Coinbase) only if the agent raises provisional credit.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_015: "4. Previous Disputes: The customer has not filed more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months"

gold[9] Staples and gold[10] Coinbase eligible_for_provisional_credit=true; gold[11]-gold[18] (Delta, Office Depot, Best Buy, Apple, Patagonia, REI, Amazon, Whole Foods: reason/amount/age/merchant-eligible) =false
instructions: "If the agent mentions provisional credit or asks about it, say: ... Please prioritize those if there's any limit."
description.notes cites "provisional_credit_max_disputes_in_period = 3", a parameter that appears in no document
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that reads the dispute history once at the start (1 prior dispute) and marks all 10 reason-eligible disputes true gets a different DB. Replaying the gold with those 8 flags set to true gives a different hash. So does a running-count agent that files in card order (Delta and Apple first).
issues.suggested_fix: State in doc_015 that disputes filed earlier in the current interaction count toward criterion 4 and that the customer chooses which disputes to file first when the limit binds, or have the customer state her priority in the opening message.

issues.summary: doc_014 lists 'reversal_of_charge' as a valid resolution_requested value, but the tool rejects it.
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that picks reversal_of_charge gets an error and has to retry. The failed call adds no record beyond the tool-name log row that the gold already creates, so the final state is unaffected.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove 'reversal_of_charge' from doc_014 or accept it in the tool.

solution_check: Reconstructed: verify, unlock and read dispute history (1 prior APPROVED dispute), give get_card_last_4_digits and have the user call it for all four accounts (last-4 values 0573/3081/3604/0652 match sha256-derived values), then file 16 disputes. Reasons, merchant contact, dates and last-4 all match gold. Provisional credit matches gold only under the running-count reading with Staples and Coinbase filed first, and the resolution fields cannot be derived from the instructions.
prior_note: The prior review called this a Blocker because of an 'unwritten cap'. The task and docs are unchanged, but under a literal running-count reading doc_015 criterion 4 does yield 2 eligible filings, so that issue is downgraded to Major ambiguity. A separate Blocker remains: the resolution_requested values are underspecified.
notes: Grading-model facts confirmed against snapshot: EnvironmentEvaluator replays gold on a fresh env and requires equal agent+user DB hashes (in this domain both toolkits share one TransactionalDB, so the two hashes are identical); _derive_read_log_allowlist logs discoverable READ calls only when gold calls them, but discoverable WRITE calls are logged by tool name even when the tool returns an error string; numbers in call_discoverable_agent_tool/call_discoverable_user_tool are parsed with parse_int=float; get_now() = 2025-11-14 03:40:00. unlock_discoverable_agent_tool is in-memory only and never hashed. Gold replay on the snapshot runs without errors. Computed eligibility: all 4 accounts opened in 2024 (>60 days); amounts $22.99-$1,299.99 are within the tier maxima; Netflix $22.99 < $25 is ineligible regardless. The Amazon (10/05) and Whole Foods (10/02) GNR purchases are >30 days old, so they are reason-eligible. Delta ($487.50 fraud) is false in gold only because of the count limit.
